L01.why: Commas on both sides of 'however' before a new clause starting 'a' usually make a comma splice, though a non-clausal reading cannot be fully ruled out.

L02.why: 'have been' needs a plural subject and the other singular/past options look more likely, but the subject is hidden.

L03.why: Plural passive 'are determined' is the outlier pairing, but voice and number both depend on the hidden subject.

L04.why: 'have been in pieces' needs a plural subject, and three options are singular, but the subject is hidden.

L05.why: 'has lain' is the only perfect form and stands apart from the progressive set, but tense depends on context.

L06.why: Past perfect 'had remained' needs a prior past reference point that may not exist, but the context is hidden.

L07.why: Past progressive 'was transposing' is the least likely tense for a completed action, but context could license it.

L08.why: 'is the' is the only non-'do' auxiliary and so most likely fails a pro-verb comparison, but a linking reading is possible.

L09.why: 'as is' is a less common comparison form than 'as do/does', but number and verb type depend on the hidden sentence.

L10.why: 'were evidently' is the only plural option among singular forms, but the subject is hidden.

L11.why: Plural passive 'were steered' combines the two outlier features, but number and voice depend on the hidden subject.

L12.why: No punctuation between 'prices' and 'a' often fuses clauses, but phrases like 'prices a buyer pays' make it possible.

L13.why: A colon right before 'cost' would usually split subject from verb, but 'cost' could be a noun after a complete clause.

L14.why: 'has been' is the only perfect form among simple be-forms, but tense and number depend on the hidden subject.

L15.why: Plural progressive active 'are misidentifying' is the odd form out, but voice and number depend on context.

L16.why: Plural active progressive is one of four symmetric number/voice combinations; no option can be ruled out without the sentence.

L17.why: No punctuation between 'spot' and 'a' often creates a run-on, but 'the spot a hiker reached' style phrasing makes it possible.

L18.why: Past perfect 'had been' needs an earlier past reference point, but the context is hidden.

L19.why: Singular active progressive 'is transporting' is the least likely form, but voice and number depend on the hidden subject.

L20.why: Past progressive 'were recording' is the only past form in a mostly present set, but context could require it.
